question.text: What will Statistics Poland's flash estimate of Poland's Q3 2026 GDP growth be?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the year-on-year real growth rate of Poland's gross domestic product in the third quarter of 2026, seasonally unadjusted and at constant prices, as first published by Statistics Poland (GUS) in its flash estimate ("Szybki szacunek produktu krajowego brutto za 3 kwartał 2026 r."), which is listed on GUS's release calendar at https://stat.gov.pl/en/release-calendar and is due in mid-November 2026. For example, if GUS states that GDP "in volume terms seasonally unadjusted was higher by 3.4% in the 3rd quarter of 2026 year-on-year", the question resolves to 3.4. Only this flash estimate counts: the later preliminary ("wstępny") estimate, the full quarterly national accounts and any subsequent revisions do not change the answer. If the figure cannot be retrieved from GUS's website, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the GUS flash estimate will be used.
question.fine_print: If GUS's flash release contains more than one year-on-year GDP growth rate, the seasonally unadjusted ("niewyrównany sezonowo") figure is the one used.

research:
I found no Q3 2026 flash figure from GUS, so the question is not settled. Bank estimates published in October run from about 3.0% (PKO BP) to 3.9% (Pekao), down from 4.1% in Q2.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The GUS November 2026 calendar page I fetched gave only a count of releases per day: 1 on 12 Nov, none on 13 Nov, 1 on 17 Nov. It did not name the releases, so I could not confirm the date of the "Szybki szacunek PKB za 3 kwartał 2026". The page may have been parsed incompletely, but the release could come on 12 Nov rather than 13 Nov. [GUS kalendarium](https://stat.gov.pl/kalendarium/13-11-2026.html), [12-11-2026](https://stat.gov.pl/kalendarium/12-11-2026.html)
- Past timing: the Q3 2025 flash came out on 13 Nov 2025 and the Q3 2023 flash on 14 Nov 2023. The Q2 2026 flash came out on 13 Aug 2026, with the preliminary estimate on 31 Aug. [GUS 13-11-2025](https://stat.gov.pl/kalendarium/13-11-2025.html), [GUS quarterly accounts](https://stat.gov.pl/obszary-tematyczne/rachunki-narodowe/kwartalne-rachunki-narodowe/)
- Latest official figures: Q2 2026 at 4.1% y/y and Q1 2026 at 3.7% y/y, both after the 16 Oct revision.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No Q3 2026 flash has been published, and I found no leak.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: The analizy.pl roundup of full-year 2026 GDP forecasts: mBank 3.9%, PKO BP 3.8%, ING 3.7%, Pekao 3.7%, Erste 3.6%, IMF 3.4%, average 3.68%. With H1 at 3.7% and 4.1%, a full-year figure of about 3.7-3.9% implies H2 growth of roughly 3.5-3.8% (my arithmetic). [analizy.pl](https://www.analizy.pl/tylko-u-nas/40940/prognozy-pkb-i-inflacji-pazdziernik-2026-ulga-w-tym-roku-wyzsze-ceny-w-przyszlym)
- 2026-10-30: Neighbours slowed in Q3. Czechia was at 1.6% y/y (from 1.8%) and Hungary at 1.5% y/y (from 1.7%). [intellinews CZ](https://www.intellinews.com/czech-gdp-grows-by-1-6-y-y-in-q1-according-to-preliminary-estimate-480616/), [intellinews HU](https://www.intellinews.com/hungary-s-gdp-growth-stalls-at-0-1-q-q-in-third-quarter-480662/)
- 2026-10-23: mBank estimates Q3 at 3.6-3.8% using the full set of Q3 data. Its quarterly forecast is 3.8%.
  - The 9% y/y fall in September construction (construction is about 6-6.5% of GDP) could take roughly 0.2pp off Q3, with that effect shifting into Q4.
  - mBank calls the weakness partly irregular contract settlements and expects a rebound in October. [mBank](https://makroekonomia.mbank.pl/475392-pazdziernik-spowolnienie-wzrostu-pkb-w-iii-kwartale)
- 2026-10-20: PKO BP says Q3 growth "most likely slowed to around 3%".
  - September industry: +4.6% y/y, or +3.3% seasonally adjusted.
  - Durable consumer goods fell 7.3%.
  - Construction fell 9% y/y, described as "surprisingly weak".
  - PPI rose to 6.1%. [wnp.pl/PAP](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/pko-bp-w-iii-kw-2026-r-wzrost-pkb-spowolnil-do-ok-3-proc,1110849.html)
- 2026-10-16: GUS revised Q2 to 4.1% (from 3.9%) and Q1 to 3.7% (from 3.5%), citing public consumption and investment. Pekao estimated Q3 at about 3.8-3.9% y/y and expects about 4% for the year. [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/polska-gospodarka-rosla-szybciej-niz-sadzono-wrzucamy-wyzszy-bieg,1109703.html)
- Earlier, about 41 days before my search: ING BSK estimated Q3 at about 3.5%. [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/ing-bsk-wzrost-pkb-w-iii-kw-2026-r-moze-wyniesc-ok-3-5-proc,1101485.html)

### 4. Base rates
- Recent figures, as reported:
  - Q1 2026: 3.5% y/y as first reported (ING, 1 Jun), later revised to 3.7%. [ING](https://think.ing.com/downloads/pdf/snap/early-year-slowdown-but-poland-still-poised-for-robust-34-growth-in-2026)
  - Q2 2026: one source says the flash was 3.8%; the preliminary estimate was 3.9% and the revised figure is 4.1%. I did not verify the 3.8% flash against GUS.
  - Full year 2025: 3.8%.
- Trend: growth of about 3.5-4.1% y/y over recent quarters. Q3 should be compared with a Q3 2025 base that is now about 0.2pp higher after the revision.
- Typical variation: in my recent examples the flash figures were 0.1-0.3pp below later revisions. Quarter-to-quarter changes in the y/y rate are usually 0.2-0.6pp.
- Consensus accuracy: Q3 2017 is the only historical case I found, a flash of 4.7% against a 4.6% consensus. I did not find a systematic dataset of flash-versus-consensus errors. [biznesradar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/27354,gus-wzrost-pkb-to-4-7-r-r-w-iii-kw-2017-wg-szybkiego-szacunku-konsensus-4-6)

### 5. Other forecasts
- Bank estimates for Q3 y/y:

| Bank | Estimate | Date |
|---|---|---|
| PKO BP | ~3.0% | 20 Oct |
| ING BSK | ~3.5% | older, about 41 days before my search |
| mBank | 3.6-3.8% | 23 Oct |
| Pekao | 3.8-3.9% | 16 Oct |

- Consensus: I found no published PAP or Bloomberg/Reuters consensus for the Q3 flash yet. A cbonds consensus page exists but showed no value. [cbonds](https://cbonds.hk/indexes/217211/)
- Prediction markets: none of the collected markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) cover Poland's GDP. I found no Manifold or Metaculus market on this.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-04 (approx.): The NBP rate decision, expected to be a hold, and possibly the November Projection with an updated GDP path. [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/czechia-to-hike-poland-on-hold-facing-sp-review-202611020628)
- 2026-11-06: S&P's sovereign rating review of Poland. It will not change the GDP figure.
- Around 11 Nov: banks will likely publish Q3 flash previews and a PAP consensus.
- 2026-11-12 or 13: the expected GUS flash release, with the date unconfirmed (see section 1).
- 2026-11-30: probably the preliminary estimate, which does not count for resolution.

I'm writing up the findings now. The main points are that the release is not out yet and bank forecasts range from about 3.0% to 3.9%.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: GUS's English release calendar (stat.gov.pl/en/release-calendar) showed no Q3 2026 flash GDP item when I checked. Its November entries were only 2 Nov (education, internal market) and a 30 Nov regional bulletin. I could not confirm the exact release date. [GUS calendar](https://stat.gov.pl/en/release-calendar)
- Past timing: the Q3 2025 flash came out on 2025-11-13 and the Q2 2026 flash on 2026-08-13. This points to about 13 Nov 2026. [GUS 13-11-2025](https://stat.gov.pl/kalendarium/13-11-2025.html), [GUS quarterly accounts](https://stat.gov.pl/obszary-tematyczne/rachunki-narodowe/kwartalne-rachunki-narodowe/)
- The latest official numbers, revised on 2026-10-16, are Q2 2026 at 4.1% y/y (was 3.9%) and Q1 2026 at 3.7% (was 3.5%). GUS said the changes came mainly from public consumption and investment (gross fixed capital formation). [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/polska-gospodarka-rosla-szybciej-niz-sadzono-wrzucamy-wyzszy-bieg,1109703.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The Q3 2026 flash has not been published, and I found no leak or early figure.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: S&P's review of Poland's sovereign rating is due Friday (6 Nov), and the central bank is expected to hold rates. Neighbours slowed in Q3: Czechia grew 1.6% y/y (Q2: 1.8%) and Hungary 1.5% y/y (Q2: 1.7%). [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/czechia-to-hike-poland-on-hold-facing-sp-review-202611020628), [Intellinews CZ](https://www.intellinews.com/czech-gdp-grows-by-1-6-y-y-in-q1-according-to-preliminary-estimate-480616/), [Intellinews HU](https://www.intellinews.com/hungary-s-gdp-growth-stalls-at-0-1-q-q-in-third-quarter-480662/)
- 2026-10-30: An analizy.pl roundup of full-year 2026 forecasts: mBank 3.9% (raised from 3.7%), PKO BP 3.8%, ING 3.7%, Pekao 3.7%, Erste 3.6%, IMF 3.4%, average 3.68%. mBank expects weak construction to pull Q3 down, with some catch-up in Q4. [analizy.pl](https://www.analizy.pl/tylko-u-nas/40940/prognozy-pkb-i-inflacji-pazdziernik-2026-ulga-w-tym-roku-wyzsze-ceny-w-przyszlym)
- 2026-10-20: PKO BP expects Q3 growth "most likely slowed to around 3%" y/y. September data:
  - Industry +4.6% y/y, or +3.3% seasonally adjusted.
  - Construction -9% y/y, or -7.2% seasonally adjusted and -7.3% m/m. PKO BP called this "surprisingly weak", following a similar miss in July.
  - Producer prices (PPI) 6.1% y/y.
  [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/pko-bp-w-iii-kw-2026-r-wzrost-pkb-spowolnil-do-ok-3-proc,1110849.html)
- 2026-10-16: Pekao said Q3 data point to "solid" growth of 3.8-3.9% y/y and put its 2026 forecast back to 4%. The 10-30 roundup lists Pekao at 3.7%, and I could not resolve that conflict. [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/polska-gospodarka-rosla-szybciej-niz-sadzono-wrzucamy-wyzszy-bieg,1109703.html)
- 2026-09-22: ING's Adam Antoniak estimated Q3 at about 3.5% y/y. He expected private consumption above 3% (Q2: 2.8%) and investment possibly above Q2's 8.4%. August retail sales were +3.8% y/y and -0.3% m/m. [wnp.pl](https://www.wnp.pl/rynki/ing-bsk-wzrost-pkb-w-iii-kw-2026-r-moze-wyniesc-ok-3-5-proc,1101485.html)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent y/y path after revisions: Q1 2026 3.7%, Q2 2026 4.1%, full-year 2025 3.8%. The Q3 2025 flash was about 3.7%. Its revised level, which is the base Q3 2026 is compared against, is not confirmed but was probably revised up by about 0.2pp like the other 2025 quarters.
- Typical moves: Poland's y/y growth usually changes by 0.2-0.6pp from one quarter to the next. Flash figures are often revised by 0.1-0.3pp later, which suggests a similar margin of uncertainty around current nowcasts.
- In 2026 the flash estimates have come in at or slightly below the later revised figures: both Q1 and Q2 were later revised up by 0.2pp.
- Calendar effects: I did not find a check on whether Q3 2026 had a different number of working days from Q3 2025. That is worth verifying, because it moves unadjusted y/y figures.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Bank nowcasts for Q3 2026 y/y:
  - PKO BP: about 3.0% (10-20)
  - Credit Agricole: 3.3%. This comes from a search summary only, and I could not verify it at the source.
  - ING: about 3.5% (09-22, before the weak September construction data)
  - mBank: about 3.6-3.8%. This figure comes from your background brief; I could not find it in a source.
  - Pekao: 3.8-3.9% (10-16)
- I found no published PAP or Parkiet consensus yet. Those surveys usually appear a few days before release.
- Prediction markets: none of the Kalshi or Polymarket listings provided cover Polish GDP. They cover South Africa, Brazil, the US, China, the eurozone and Japan, plus unrelated chess markets. I found no Manifold or Metaculus equivalent.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-06: S&P's rating review of Poland. This would not change the GDP data.
- Early to mid November: the central bank (NBP) rate decision and its November projection, plus the bank consensus surveys published ahead of the flash.
- 2026-11-13 (likely): GUS publishes the Q3 2026 flash estimate; check the GUS calendar to confirm the date. The headline unadjusted y/y figure decides the question. The preliminary estimate at the end of November does not count.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 10 days. The GUS flash is due around 12-13 November 2026.

(b) **Latest known value:** Q2 2026 GDP grew 4.1% y/y, as revised on 16 October 2026. The Q2 flash on 13 August was about 3.8% and was later revised up. Q1 2026 stands at 3.7% y/y after revision.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 4.0%, roughly a repeat of Q2.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** Q3 monthly data point to a slowdown, led by weak construction (-9% y/y in September) and slower retail sales, partly offset by strong industry. That suggests about 3.5-3.8%.

(e) **Historical variation:** the y/y rate usually moves 0.2-0.6pp from one quarter to the next. Flash surprises against consensus are typically 0.1-0.3pp, and occasionally 0.5pp.

(f) **Expert expectations:**
- mBank, using the full Q3 data set: 3.6-3.8%.
- Pekao: 3.8-3.9%.
- ING: about 3.5%, an older estimate.
- PKO BP: about 3.0%.
- Full-year forecasts of about 3.7-3.9% imply second-half growth of about 3.5-3.8%.
- No prediction market covers this.
- I put the median at about 3.6%.

(g) **Scenarios:**
- **Low:** construction and investment collapse further, inventories drag, and calendar effects work against Q3. This could put the flash near 2.8-3.0%, in line with PKO.
- **High:** public consumption and investment strength, the driver of the recent upward revisions, carries into Q3 and inventories add to growth. This could give 4.2-4.4%.
